---
title: "Spectral engine"
---

## Blending as spectra

With **Blend Domain = Waveform** (default) the echo adds up the traces' audio. That's exact, but two memories
that aren't aligned in time can cancel or comb-filter each other; the lower the **Activation Power**, the more
memories blend and the more it happens.

With **Blend Domain = Spectral** the echo is built from short-time spectra instead: for every ~43 ms frame, each
active memory's magnitude spectrum is weighted by its activation and summed, and every frequency takes the phase
of the memory that is loudest there. Memories blend without cancelling (two opposite-phase copies of a tone,
which cancel completely as waveforms, add up spectrally). With a single memory the result is identical to the
waveform echo.

- **Spectral Voices** (1–32): how many of the most active memories are analysed per frame. Fewer is cheaper and
  clearer.
- Frames are about 43 ms long, so changes in the echo fade in over about that time. There is no added latency.
- In spectral mode, voice detune, wow/flutter and Loop are ignored.
- It costs more CPU: roughly 3–4 % of one core per instance, against well under 1 % for waveform blending.

## Spectral freeze

**Spectral Freeze** holds the echo's current spectrum as a drone. Its partials keep turning at their measured
frequencies (with a little jitter so it doesn't sound static), so it keeps its pitch even after memory is cleared.
Hold MIDI note *base + 2* to freeze while the note is down.

## Stretch

**Length Mismatch = Stretch** plays traces recorded at another length through a phase vocoder, so they fit the
new length without changing pitch. It uses the spectral engine even when Blend Domain is Waveform.

## Grain memories

Set **Sync** to Free and **Trace Length (Free)** to 15–50 ms, raise **Memory Capacity** into the thousands and
turn **Self Match** off: every grain is answered by the most similar earlier grains, a granular cloud that follows
what you play. **Max Active Traces** keeps it affordable. Try the **20 Grain Cloud** preset.
